traps.shape: the reported route: the DOM scanner validates only the first child of a style element, so later text children are serialised raw and a browser reparses the smuggled markup as elements
traps.reason_to_dismiss: NekoHTML is assumed to return one text child for style content, and any element children are still walked, so reading only the first child is taken to cover the element's CSS
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code (the advisory route)

traps.shape: the lexical on-site URL expression accepts a backslash; a browser normalises a leading separator pair containing a backslash to a protocol-relative reference, so an on-site value becomes another origin
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the existing negative lookahead for two forward slashes looks like it already refuses protocol-relative references

traps.shape: non-void elements listed as allowed-empty are serialised self-closed in XHTML output; a browser holds the element open and absorbs the content that follows the submitted fragment
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the shipped policies remove script and iframe and HTML output already closes non-void elements, so the short default require-closing list is assumed sufficient
